A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OBCD research work. Their readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated methods and proofs.

before.justification: V2 reports original numerical experiments on L0-regularized SPCA, L1-regularized SPCA and nonnegative PCA in Section 6 and Appendix J.

after.justification: V4 reports original numerical experiments on the same three optimization tasks in Section 5 and Appendix G, including objective values and convergence curves.

M1.justification: The core orthogonality-preserving row update, majorization subproblem and breakpoint solver remain. However, v4 removes the entire greedy working-set component: WSS-SV and WSS-OR, specified in v2 Algorithm 2 and Appendix D. Only random and cyclic selection strategies remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate L0-SPCA, L1-SPCA and nonnegative PCA on the same ten real-world and synthetic datasets. CnnCal in v4 corresponds to the retained CnnCaltech data. The added capped-L1 example is not evaluated.

E2.justification: V4 adds RADMM to L0-SPCA and nonnegative-PCA comparisons, and RSSM to L1-SPCA. Greedy OBCD variants and baseline-plus-OBCD hybrid comparisons disappear. SPM/PSM corresponds across naming changes. V4's nonnegative-PCA prose names LADMM while Table 3 says ADMM, leaving that particular comparator identity unresolved.

E3.justification: Tables switch from relative objective gaps to absolute objectives and replace regularization, component-count and timing grids. Table 1 changes from 30 to 40 seconds, although v4's prose still says 30. L1 comparisons replace shared identity initialization with random baseline starts versus identity OBCD starts. Nonnegative-PCA feasibility reporting drops orthogonality error, and new curves use an objective augmented by a 1000-weighted nonnegativity penalty.

E4.justification: V2's analyses of working-set selection effectiveness and whether ten seconds of OBCD refinement improves LADMM, SPM or ManPG solutions are removed, including their supporting Appendix J comparisons. The rotation-versus-reflection examples in Appendix C.1 remain; the additional benchmark curves do not replace the removed component and refinement analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. V2's (+) markers indicate a fixed objective-improvement threshold, not statistical significance.

E6.justification: The numerical record changes substantially across all three tasks. For MNIST L0-SPCA with r=20 and lambda=10, v2 Table 1 reports an OBCD-R relative gap of 6.25e+04; v4 reports an absolute objective of 199.896. Changed metrics and settings prevent direct performance comparison. New baseline scores and curve entries replace extensive greedy and hybrid results.

T1.justification: V4 adds an all-k completeness corollary, an O(1/epsilon) bound under a squared Riemannian-stationarity criterion, and explicit finite, linear and sublinear last-iterate rates with supporting proofs. It revises boundedness assumptions, subgradient estimates and the finite-length argument. Conversely, v2's cyclic-selection complexity guarantee and greedy-selection theory are removed. The existing block-stationarity complexity result and relocated breakpoint derivation are retained.

C1.justification: V4 expands the central theoretical claim from strong limit-point convergence to explicit non-ergodic convergence rates. It removes the first-monotone-greedy-method claim and greedy working-set extensions from the stated contributions. Feasibility, inexpensive row updates and stronger-than-critical stationarity remain central.

C2.justification: V4 qualifies the previously mentioned local-subproblem fallback with an explicit descent requirement and clearer tractability limits in Remark 2.4. It removes v2's explanation that greedy selection can underperform on nonnegative PCA because zero is an unsuitable subgradient choice. The main interpretation linking lower objectives to stronger stationary points remains.

D1.justification: Appendix G.2 newly specifies unit-Frobenius normalization of the data matrix; the PDFs do not establish whether this was previously implemented but undocumented. V2's nonnegative initialization recipe and greedy candidate-sampling details disappear. MATLAB/C++ implementation, hardware, proximal parameter, L0 reporting threshold and the supplemental-code statement remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands to landing methods and Riemannian block majorization-minimization, with additional discussion of work by Ablin, Cheung, Li, Lyu and others. V4 also withdraws v2's blanket assertions that no existing BCD method handles the nonsmooth problem and that this is its first BCD application, substantially revising research positioning.

P1.justification: V4 extensively rewrites the abstract, related work and convergence narrative, moves PCA applications into an introductory subsection, and introduces main-text notation explanations. It consolidates the breakpoint solver and its proof in Appendix B and reorganizes the remaining appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond scientific additions.

P2.justification: Dense full-page rank/time tables are replaced by compact comparison panels and a much larger collection of convergence plots. Comparator columns, legends, axes and captions change; Algorithm 1 is reformatted and Algorithm 2 is removed. The geometric Figure 2 and Jacobi-Givens code listing are retained with relocation or formatting changes.

improvement.justification: V4's clearer organization and added RADMM/RSSM comparisons are useful. However, replacing v2's shared L1 initialization with unequal starts weakens comparative control. The revised KL proof also substitutes the global infimum for the limit-point objective without establishing equality, unlike v2's limit-point-based formulation (v4 Appendix F.4 versus v2 Appendix G.3). These unresolved issues limit confidence in the expanded theoretical and empirical support, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
